title: Canonical finite-free tensor comparison for derived products and strict towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $a:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ as an $R$-module sheaf for a finite integer $d\geq0$. Use the unbounded module derived categories $D(R),D(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $C=-\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $\operatorname{Tow}(R)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, and similarly for $S$. Let $C^{\operatorname{Tow}}:D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(S))$ be induced by termwise tensor, which is exact under the finite-free hypothesis. Write $L_R,L_S$ for total right derived inverse limit with its functorial Roos triangles [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

For every countable family $(M_n)$ in $D(R)$, the canonical projection comparison $C(\prod_n^D M_n)\to\prod_n^D C(M_n)$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_X:C L_R X\xrightarrow{\sim}L_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\qquad(X\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))).$$
It is the total derived-functor comparison induced by the ordinary limit/tensor comparison. It identifies the entire functorial Roos triangles, including the connecting arrows, under the canonical derived-product comparison and the cochain shift comparison of $C$. For a strict augmented tower of complexes $z_n:M\to X_n$, its canonical derived-limit augmentation $z:M\to L_R X$ satisfies $\lambda_X C(z)=z'$, where $z':CM\to L_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ is induced by the termwise augmented tower $C(z_n)$. These comparisons are independent of a basis and natural in maps of entire augmented towers; no exactness of countable products of sheaves and no boundedness of the complexes are assumed.

proof.text: Put $F=-\otimes_R S$ on module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and $U=\operatorname{Res}_{R\to S}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-sheaf], $R$ and $S$ are commutative ring objects of abelian sheaves and $a$ is a ring-object map; their reconstructed section-ring sheaves are $R,S$ and $a$ again, since the multiplication extends the objectwise one. By [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction], the equivalences preserving underlying sheaves identify the internal adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_a\dashv\operatorname{Res}_a$ of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] with $F\dashv U$, units and counits included. By [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products], $U$ is conservative and preserves limits. Since restriction changes only the action, it is exact and detects zero objects and exactness. Choose a basis only for this proof. The given isomorphism $R^{\oplus d}\cong S$ is one of underlying sheaves, hence an internal $R$-module isomorphism. Transported along these identifications, the coordinate isomorphism [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] identifies $UF(M)$ naturally with $M^d$. Thus $F$ is exact: applying $U$ to an $F$-image of a short exact sequence gives its finite direct sum. The exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies termwise $F$ with $C$ and supplies its cochain shift comparison. This is also the derived tensor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], since exact $F$ sends a K-flat resolution to a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness in tower categories is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so the same argument supplies $C^{\operatorname{Tow}}$.

proof.text: Let $\phi:F(\prod_n A_n)\to\prod_n F(A_n)$ be the ordinary product comparison, defined by its projections. After $U$ and the coordinates of [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates], transported as in Step 1, it is exactly $(\prod_n A_n)^d\to\prod_n(A_n^d)$, sending a tuple of families to the family of tuples; its inverse interchanges the same two indices. It is therefore invertible. Likewise the canonical map $\beta_T:F(\lim T)\to\lim F^{\operatorname{Tow}}T$ is invertible: its underlying map is $(\lim T)^d\to\lim(T^d)$, with inverse taking the $d$ compatible coordinate families separately. These are isomorphisms of $S$-modules because the original maps are $S$-linear and $U$ is conservative and preserves limits [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products]. Their definitions by projections show that $\phi$ and $\beta$ are natural and do not depend on the chosen basis. The argument applies degreewise to complexes and commutes with differentials.

proof.text: Use [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] for functorial K-injective resolutions with injective terms over $R$ and $S$. For towers use [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] with the small category $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the constant coefficient sheaf, and apply the same resolution theorem on that small site. On modules and on towers, $U$ carries K-injectives to K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]: its left adjoint is $F$, respectively termwise $F$, already proved exact. If $I$ is K-injective over $R$, then $UF I\cong I^d$ is K-injective by the product theorem [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], also for $d=0$. This assertion applies equally in the abelian tower category. We do not assert that $F I$ is K-injective over $S$.

proof.text: Represent $M_n$ by complexes and resolve them as $M_n\to I_n$ over $R$; choose $r_n:F I_n\to J_n$ K-injective resolutions over $S$. The complexes $I_n,J_n$ compute the two derived products by [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]. Each $U(r_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives: its source is $I_n^d$ and its target is K-injective by the preceding exact-adjoint argument. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] it is a homotopy equivalence. Products of these homotopy equivalences are homotopy equivalences, since the inverse and both homotopies are specified separately at every projection. Consequently $F(\prod I_n)\xrightarrow{\phi}\prod F I_n\xrightarrow{\prod r_n}\prod J_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism: after $U$, its first arrow is an isomorphism and its second a homotopy equivalence. Its $n$th projection is $r_nF(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, so its derived image is the canonical projection comparison required in the statement. In particular this also proves that $\prod F I_n$ represents the derived product of the $F M_n$.

proof.text:
For a representative strict tower complex $X$, choose $q:X\to I$ K-injective with injective tower terms, and $r:F^{\operatorname{Tow}} I\to J$ a K-injective $S$-tower resolution with injective tower terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $L_R X$ is represented by $\lim I$, and $L_S C^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ by $\lim J$ using the resolution $rF(q)$. Define $\lambda_X$ by the chain map
$$F(\lim I)\xrightarrow{\beta_I}\lim F^{\operatorname{Tow}}I\xrightarrow{\lim r}\lim J.$$
This is precisely the ordinary limit/tensor comparison followed by the right-derived comparison unit on the image tower, with the inverse of the derived image of $F(q)$. Thus it is the total derived-functor comparison specified in the item, rather than a choice of an isomorphism between abstract cones. Functorial resolutions make this construction natural on complexes.

proof.text: The map $U^{\operatorname{Tow}}r$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective $R$-tower complexes: its source is $I^d$ and its target is K-injective by Step 3. Hence it is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Applying the additive functor $\lim$ preserves its inverse and homotopies. Since $U$ commutes with limits [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products], $U(\lim r)$ is a homotopy equivalence. Exact conservative $U$ detects quasi-isomorphisms, so the map in Step 5 is a quasi-isomorphism. The natural comparison thus descends through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to a natural isomorphism on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))$: both its source and target functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. It is independent of resolutions. Indeed comparisons between two source resolutions are unique up to homotopy under $X$ by the cited K-injective Hom bijection; $F$ preserves these homotopies. The same bijection for target resolutions under $FX$ makes the resulting square commute up to homotopy. Applying $\lim$, and naturality of $\beta$, therefore give the same derived map.

proof.text: To check the entire specified Roos triangles, work with the injective-term resolutions $I,J$ of Step 5. Here is the elementary injectivity calculation needed for their ordinary product sequences. For any injective tower $T$, let $P_n(A)$ be $A$ at levels $m\le n$, zero at $m>n$, with identity nonzero transitions. There is a monomorphism $P_n(A)\to P_{n+1}(A)$. The map $P_n(T_n)\to T$ whose component at $n$ is the identity extends across this monomorphism by injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its component at $n+1$ is a section $\sigma_n:T_n\to T_{n+1}$ of the transition $t_n$. In each cochain degree, $1-s$ on $\prod T_n$ consequently has a right inverse: for an input $(x_n)$ set $y_1=0$ and $y_{n+1}=\sigma_n(y_n-x_n)$. Each coordinate is a finite sum of coordinate morphisms, and $y_n-t_ny_{n+1}=x_n$. The product universal property therefore defines the asserted right inverse without any product-exactness hypothesis.

proof.text:
The kernel of $1-s$ consists exactly of compatible families, hence is $\lim T$ by the limit universal property. Applied degreewise to $I$ and $J$, Step 7 therefore gives short exact sequences of complexes
$$0\to\lim I\to P_I\xrightarrow{1-s_I}P_I\to0,\qquad 0\to\lim J\to P_J\xrightarrow{1-s_J}P_J\to0,$$
where $P_I=\prod I_n$ and $P_J=\prod J_n$. Their products represent the derived products: evaluation of a K-injective tower is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], and then apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]. The natural short-exact-sequence triangles [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] are the resolved functorial Roos triangles used to compute $L_R,L_S$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. This identifies the construction of these triangles, not merely their objects.

Apply exact $F$ to the first short exact sequence of Step 8. Map it to the second by $\ell=(\lim r)\beta_I$ on the left and $b=(\prod r_n)\phi_I$ on both product terms. The left square commutes after each projection by the definition of $\beta_I$. For the right square, if $t_n:I_{n+1}\to I_n$ and $u_n:J_{n+1}\to J_n$ are the transitions, then
$$\mathrm{pr}_n bF(s_I)=r_nF(t_n)F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=u_nr_{n+1}F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=\mathrm{pr}_n s_Jb.$$
Thus $bF(1-s_I)=(1-s_J)b$. By Step 7 the first sequence is split in every degree (a degreewise right inverse of $1-s_I$ gives the splitting), so [lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison] gives $\delta_I=Q(d_I)$ for its cochain boundary $d_I$, built from the splitting. Additive $F$ carries the splitting to a splitting of the $F$-image, whose cochain boundary is therefore $F(d_I)$, and the same lemma gives its connecting map as $Q(F(d_I))$. Naturality of $\varphi$ and the shift compatibility (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], with $\tau$ the identity, identify $C(\delta_I)$ with $Q(F(d_I))$; call $\xi$ this shift comparison. Naturality of the connecting map in [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] for the morphism $(\ell,b,b)$ of short exact sequences then gives
$$\ell[1]\,\xi\,C(\delta_I)=\delta_J b.$$
Under Step 4, $b$ is exactly the canonical derived-product comparison, and under Step 5, $\ell$ is $\lambda_X$. This proves compatibility with all arrows, including the connecting arrow; it does not invoke uniqueness of cone fillers.

proof.text:
For completeness identify the augmentation without discarding its strict data. The constant-tower functor $\Delta_R$ is exact by levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] and is left adjoint to $\lim$ by the limit universal property, with $\lim\Delta_RM=M$. Hence $\lim I$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(\Delta_RM,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(\Delta_RM,I)$ through $q$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(M,\lim I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(M,\lim I)$; the ordinary adjunction respects homotopies, so it gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_D(\Delta_RM,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(M,L_RX)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], natural in both variables and independent of $q$ by the same Hom bijection. This is the derived adjunction $D(\Delta_R)\dashv L_R$, with $D(\Delta_R)$ the termwise functor of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For a strict chain map $z_\bullet:\Delta_R M\to X$, its canonical derived adjunct $z$ is thus represented by
$$M\xrightarrow{\lim(qz_\bullet)}\lim I.$$
The $S$-augmentation $z'$ is represented, using the target resolution $rF(q)$, by
$$FM\xrightarrow{\lim(rF(qz_\bullet))}\lim J.$$
Naturality of $\beta$ and its defining projection equations identify the latter chain map with $(\lim r)\beta_I F(\lim(qz_\bullet))$. This is precisely $\lambda_X C(z)=z'$.

proof.text: A map of entire augmented towers is a pair $h:M\to N$, $v:X\to Y$ satisfying $v_nz_n=w_nh$ for every $n$. Functorial $q,r$, naturality of $\beta,\phi$, and the componentwise equality in Step 10 make its augmentation comparison square commute. Step 9 gives the corresponding natural morphism of whole Roos triangles. No definition of these maps used a basis: $\phi,\beta$ were defined by projections, and $\lambda$ by their derived comparison units. The basis was used solely to prove those maps invertible and to prove the K-injective homotopy-equivalence tests. Thus all comparisons are basis independent. Empty finite coordinates ($d=0$), zero complexes, and arbitrary unbounded degrees obey the same formulas. No step takes cohomology through an unresolved infinite product.
